candidates.original_title: Subliminal instrumental conditioning demonstrated in the human brain
candidates.description: Participants learned to adjust Go/NoGo responses in line with subliminally presented rewarding and punishing cues, constituting instrumental conditioning without conscious awareness of the cues.
candidates.citation_sentence: Experiment 2 was designed to be conducted only in the event of Experiment 1 replicating the effect found in Pessiglione et al. (2008).
candidates.notes: Strong Bayes factor evidence for absence of learning (BH(0,0.7) = .11, RRB < 1/6) when aware trials were excluded. Authors explicitly state this challenges the original finding and that apparent evidence for learning in Experiment 1 was likely due to inadequate exclusion of aware trials.

candidates.original_title: Subliminal instrumental conditioning demonstrated in the human brain
candidates.description: Participants learned to adjust Go/NoGo responses in line with subliminally presented rewarding and punishing cues, constituting instrumental conditioning without conscious awareness of the cues.
candidates.citation_sentence: Experiment 1 aims to directly replicate unconscious instrumental conditioning found in Pessiglione et al. (2008).
candidates.notes: Authors found significant learning in the conditioning task (replicating the original) but also found significant group-level awareness on PDT2, contradicting the original's claim of unconsciousness. Mixed signals within one experiment: learning replicated but awareness was present, preventing the claim of unconscious conditioning. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Subliminal instrumental conditioning demonstrated in the human brain
candidates.description: Subliminal rewarding and punishing cues produce instrumental Go/NoGo conditioning without conscious awareness of the cues.
candidates.citation_sentence: Here, we attempt to replicate the original result of Pessiglione et al. (2008), leveraging the developments in the field of unconscious processing to apply a more robust statistical approach (Experiment 1), and a more rigorous methodology (Experiment 2).
candidates.notes: The experiment introduced methodological changes to improve awareness assessment and found strong evidence for the absence of learning on unaware trials; the authors state that this challenges the original finding.
